item.content: {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=computational+boundaries+persistent+identity+memory+continuity+philosophy&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Seedance 2.0: Prospects and reflections on the evolution from “tool” to “creator”\", \"abstract\": null, \"doi\": null, \"pmid\": \"PMC13673547\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13673547\", \"source\": \"PMC\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13673547/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13673547/pdf/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13673547\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13673547?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Digital pharmaka and the crisis of subjectivation: a longitudinal phenomenological study on the educational use of technology in higher education through the philosophy of Bernard Stiegler.\", \"abstract\": \"This study investigates the ambivalent effects of digital technologies on the subjectivation processes of university students, drawing on Bernard Stiegler's philosophy of technics and the concept of the pharmakon, technology as both remedy and poison. Using a longitudinal qualitative design grounded in interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA), the research examines how digital technologies - including smartphones, social media, and AI tools - affect students' attention, memory, desires, and sense of self over an academic semester. Data from three waves of in-depth interviews and reflective journals with twelve undergraduates reveal six interrelated themes: (1) from habitual engagement to cognitive embodiment: the internalization of digital technology; (2) the fragmentation of cognitive focus: the collapse of attention regimes; (3) loss of control and addiction-like engagement…
